title: BFT/CFT Reconciliation
purpose: Document the gap between seminar assumptions (PBFT) and implementation (Raft CFT), and justify the design decision

seminar_assumptions.institutional_argument: §3.4.2 argues non-collusion based on BFT bound

gap_analysis.nature_of_gap: Seminar assumes Byzantine fault tolerance; implementation provides only crash fault tolerance
what_raft_does_not_tolerate: Equivocation (sending different messages to different peers)
gap_analysis.seminar_error: Table 4.2 lists 'PBFT' for Fabric, which was factually incorrect - PBFT was removed in Fabric v1.0 (2017). Fabric has used Raft since v1.4 (2019).

current_gap_to_bft.complexity: High - requires Fabric major version upgrade

justification_for_raft.decision: Keep Raft CFT, revise threat model
rationale: 1. Consortium participants are identified institutions (licensed banks under CBN supervision)
2. Regulatory observer maintains real-time visibility of all transactions
3. Reputational exposure and regulatory sanction raise the cost of institutional collusion beyond technical capability
4. Byzantine tolerance protects against anonymous validators; consortium validators are accountable entities
5. Seminar §3.4.3 already argues institutional accountability - this argument does real work here

threat_model_revision.assumption: Orderer operators are accountable institutions under regulatory supervision with strong reputational incentives against malicious behavior

endorsement_policy_analysis.issue: With non-endorsing RegulatoryObserver, this requires ALL 3 endorsers to sign
endorsement_policy_analysis.fault_tolerance_at_endorsement: Zero - one endorser down halts commits
endorsement_policy_analysis.recommendation: Consider MAJORITY over 3 endorsing orgs only (2 of 3) for fault tolerance at endorsement layer

chapter_3.§3.4.1: Replace BFT assumption with CFT + institutional accountability argument
chapter_3.§3.4.2: Strengthen institutional non-collusion argument as primary defense, not secondary

chapter_4.Table_4.2: Change 'PBFT' to 'Raft (CFT)' and document fault tolerance properties accurately

chapter_6.limitations: Explicitly state that Byzantine behavior by orderers is outside the threat model

summary.fault_tolerance_guarantee: Tolerates ⌊(n-1)/2⌋ crash failures with n orderers
summary.defense: Institutional accountability, regulatory supervision, embedded observer
